name: Deepfield
author: gurvinny
description:
Deepfield replaces Pelican Panel's default look with a cosmic-atmospheric UI in two matching palettes, dark and light. A canvas-based three-tier parallax starfield drifts behind every page with mouse-driven motion and pooled meteors, layered over a slow-moving nebula fog. Aurora-gradient accents (cyan -> teal -> violet) live on primary buttons, active sidebar nav, focus rings, and status badges - never washed out because the sidebar and modals stay heavily tinted and readable.

The in-server console gets special treatment: a CRT monitor top bar, optional phosphor bloom and scanlines, and Start / Restart / Stop pills that glow in their own status colors. The xterm.js palette is patched at runtime so terminal colors match the theme (four presets, including a 1:1 Minecraft vanilla palette for Paper / Forge / CurseForge servers).

Skins all three Filament panels - admin, app, and server - with premium self-hosted typography (Orbitron display, Space Grotesk UI, JetBrains Mono code). No CDN calls, no Google Fonts round-trip. Every effect is Filament-configurable through a native settings page: starfield density, nebula on/off + hue, CRT bloom, terminal palette, scanline density, audio cues, reduce-motion. Values persist to .env. Respects prefers-reduced-motion automatically.

Ships two palettes rather than one: the deep-cosmic dark theme and a cool observatory-white light theme, built from a single set of colour tokens so both read as the same design. The panel's own theme switcher chooses between them and each user's choice is theirs to keep - Deepfield only sets the default. The console screen stays dark in light mode by default, so the terminal palettes stay valid. Coexists with Theme Customizer: its component colours can be handed over with one toggle.
